info.title: Integr8 Plus API
info.description:
Multi-tenant field operations platform.

## Versioning

Every path is prefixed `/v1`. Nothing breaking ships inside a version:
a field may be added, an enum may gain a value, an endpoint may appear.
Removing a field, renaming one, narrowing a type or making an optional
field required is a `/v2`.

This is not a style rule. A signed desktop binary and an App Store
build cannot be force-updated, so at any moment some traffic comes from
software written months ago and still under support.

## Headers

Every response carries `x-request-id`; quote it when reporting a problem.
Every response carries `min-supported-client`, the oldest client build
this deployment serves (currently `0.1.0`).
Send `x-client-version` and `x-client-app` so the server can tell you to
update before a call fails for a reason you cannot diagnose.

Mutating endpoints marked idempotent accept `Idempotency-Key`. Replaying
a request with the same key returns the original response and repeats no
effect.

bearerAuth.description: The access token from `POST /v1/auth/sign-in`. Fifteen minutes.

websiteKeyAuth.description: A website key created by Integr8 staff. Keep it in the company website server environment; never expose it to browser code.

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and password
post.description: Returns a token pair for one company, plus every company this person belongs to. For `clientApp: mobile` the pair also carries the offline grant that lets the phone open with no network for seven days (`offlineGrant`, `offlineGrantExpiresAt`). A wrong password, an unknown address and an identity with no company are all the same failure, deliberately: distinguishing them would turn this endpoint into a way of testing which addresses are customers.

offlineGrant.description: Mobile only. A signed grant (EdDSA JWT, `typ: offline`) the phone keeps and checks with no network; replaces the previous one. Absent for the desktop and web apps.

offlineGrantExpiresAt.description: When the offline grant ends: seven days by default, never after the session does.

post.summary: Email a 6-digit sign-in code
post.description: Emails a one-time 6-digit code that signs in through `/v1/auth/magic-link/complete`. Always answers 202 the same way, whether or not the address has an account: an endpoint that answered differently for a known address would be a free customer-list oracle. One code per address per minute and five per hour, counted the same for unknown addresses (429 `auth.rate_limited`). The path keeps its old name so nothing inside `/v1` changes; `redirectTo` is accepted and ignored, because the email carries a code and no link.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair
